events.region: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon; South Washington Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow
flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 4 AM PST
Friday.

* IMPACTS...Major flooding, up to two feet above ground level,
during high tides is expected along the immediate coast as well
as low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of
the coastal rivers.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS... Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal
overflow flooding of low-lying areas is expected due to high
tides. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert for
rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life
and property.

events.region: Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico AND USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N; Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N...
Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...

* At 325 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. This a strong
thunderstorm was located along the coast Isabela and Quebradillas
over the Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM zones,
moving northwest at 10 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from
10 NM to 19.5N and Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10
NM.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 60 mph
possible.

* WHERE...Del Norte Coast.

* WHEN...From Monday evening through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are possible. Travel could be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles. Wind gusts will be
particularly strong along windward ridges and exposed coastal
headlands.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High winds aloft along the Del Norte Coast
have the potential to mix down to the surface leading to stronger
winds, especially Tuesday morning.

events.region: Northern Park; Red Lodge Foothills; Judith Gap; Paradise Valley; Livingston Area; Beartooth Foothills; Northern Sweet Grass; Melville Foothills; Southern Wheatland
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Areas of dense fog producing visibility of a quarter mile or
less.

* WHERE...Portions of central and south central Montana, especially
on the east side of the mountains.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel will be impacted by poor visibility and locally
slick roads. Highways which will be impacted by fog include US-212
near Red Lodge, I-90 over Bozeman Pass, US-191 through Melville,
and other routes along the eastern slopes of the mountains.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Visibilities may improve a bit this afternoon,
but will become worse again after sunset. A combination of fog and
low clouds will remain in place until winds become westerly on
Monday.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Isolated minor coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Wave run-up may approach the dunes along narrow
beaches. Beach equipment, such as umbrellas and chairs, could
be moved by waves. Vehicles driving along narrow beaches may
experience higher water levels. Elevated water levels may also
occur across the Laguna Madre and South Bay, and along State
Highway 4 west of Boca Chica State Park.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide
at 340 PM today and 452 PM Monday.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Lake effect snow expected. Total snow accumulations between
2 and 5 inches. Up to 8 inches underneath the dominant lake effect
snow band.

* WHERE...Baraga, Northern Houghton, Ontonagon, and Southern Houghton
Counties.

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 11 AM EST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. Moderate to heavy
snowfall rates will cause visibility to fall below 1 mile at times.
The hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A dominant lake effect band with heavy
snowfall rates up to 1 inch per hour at times will yield an area of
6-8 inches of snow. Medium confidence in exact placement of this
band. Area of focus is between Ontonagon, Painesdale, Herman,
Covington, and Bruce Crossing. Heaviest snowfall expected to remain
south of Houghton.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A building trade-wind swell will produce a
high risk of rip currents along east facing reefs. Surf and rip
current risk will also be elevated along north facing reefs, but
remain just below High Surf Advisory and High Rip Current Risk
levels.
